set.settings.integrations.panelTokensHelp: For scripts, CI or tools without a browser: send the token in the HTTP header “Authorization: Bearer”. You decide which zones it applies to, whether it is read-only and when it expires – it can never do more than your own account.
set.settings.integrations.apiInfoP2: A panel token is just another way to sign in to the same API: instead of a session cookie you send “Authorization: Bearer <complete token>”. Settings, user administration and credentials (password, 2FA, passkeys, tokens, webhooks) always require a browser login.
set.panelTokens.empty: No API tokens yet. You only need tokens for scripts, CI or other tools without a browser.
set.panelTokens.permManageHint: May change records, DNSSEC and zone settings in the allowed zones – never more than your user account may.
set.panelTokens.permReadHint: Read requests (GET) only. Every change is rejected with HTTP 403.
set.panelTokens.zonesAllHint: Follows your zone permissions automatically – including zones assigned to you later.
set.panelTokens.zonesAllAdminHint: Applies to all zones on all servers, including zones created later.
set.panelTokens.zonesNoneAvailable: No zones are assigned to you – an administrator has to grant you zones first.
set.panelTokens.zonesLoadPartial: Unreachable: {{servers}} – the zone list may be incomplete. You can add missing zones by hand below.
set.panelTokens.zonesLoadFailed: The zone list could not be loaded. You can add zones by hand below.
set.panelTokens.zonesTooMany: {{count}} more matches – please refine the filter.
set.panelTokens.zonesSelectAtLeastOne: Please select at least one zone.
set.panelTokens.fieldNameHint: What is the token for? e.g. “CI deploy example.com”
set.panelTokens.expiryNeverWarning: Tokens without expiry are not recommended in company environments – rotate them regularly instead.
set.panelTokens.expiryEditHint: A new validity period starts today.
set.panelTokens.expiredResumeHint: Expired – choose a new validity period under “Edit” to keep using it.
set.panelTokens.adminInactiveHint: Your account is no longer an administrator – this token's admin permission has no effect.
set.panelTokens.broadAccessHint: All zones and no expiry – best restrict it to the zones needed and set an expiry.
set.panelTokens.allowAdminHint: Allows creating, importing and deleting zones, managing templates, reading the user list and the audit log. Settings, user administration and credentials never work with a token – they always require a browser login.
set.panelTokens.allowAdminNeedsAllZones: Only possible if the token applies to all zones.
set.panelTokens.pauseConfirm: Pause token “{{name}}”? It is kept and can be activated again later.
set.panelTokens.revokeConfirm: Permanently revoke token “{{name}}”? Scripts using it will get HTTP 401 afterwards.
set.panelTokens.scopeNotice: A token can never do more than your user account: if an administrator removes your zone permissions, the token loses access too.
set.panelTokens.createdBody: The token is shown only now. Store it safely (e.g. in a password manager or as a CI secret) – afterwards only its beginning is visible.
set.users.apiTokensHint: Active, paused and expired tokens. You can revoke them but not change them.
set.users.apiTokensRevokeAllConfirm: Revoke all {{count}} API tokens of {{user}}? Scripts using these tokens will stop working.
